import pytest
from target import unescapeHTML

# Helper to compare expected output with actual for a variety of inputs
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "input_str,expected",
    [
        # Basic known entities
        ("&", "&"),
        ("<", "<"),
        (">", ">"),
        (""", '"'),
        ("'", "'"),
        # Multiple entities in one string
        ("A & B < C > D", "A & B < C > D"),
        # Entities adjacent to other text
        ("Start&Middle<End", "Start&Middle<End"),
        # No entity (no semicolon) – should remain unchanged
        ("Fish & Chips", "Fish & Chips"),
        ("&amp", "&amp"),
        # Entity with extra characters after semicolon – only the entity part should be transformed
        ("&foo", "&foo"),
        ("&foo;", "&foo;"),
        # Edge case where a stray '&' appears before a valid entity
        ("&&", "&&"),
        # Empty string
        ("", ""),
        # String with only an ampersand and semicolon (invalid entity) – unchanged
        ("&;", "&;"),
    ],
)
def test_unescapeHTML_basic_cases(input_str, expected):
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected


def test_unescapeHTML_none_input():
    assert unescapeHTML(None) is None


def test_unescapeHTML_type_assertion():
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
        unescapeHTML(123)  # not a compat_str (i.e., not a str)


def test_unescapeHTML_overlapping_entities():
    """
    This tests the scenario that could be affected by the regex change:
    The old regex stops at the first ';' after an '&', while the new regex
    could greedily consume up to the last ';' in the string.
    The expected behavior (old spec) is to only replace the first valid entity.
    """
    # Input with two semicolons; only the first entity should be transformed.
    input_str = "&foo;"
    # Old behavior: '&' -> '&', leaving 'foo;'
    expected = "&foo;"
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected

    # More complex case with multiple entities and extra semicolons
    input_str = "X &Y;Z <W;"
    # Expected: only '&' and '<' are transformed, others remain
    expected = "X &Y;Z <W;"
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected


def test_unescapeHTML_no_entities():
    # Strings without any '&...;' pattern should be returned unchanged
    inputs = [
        "plain text",
        "&&&&",
        "&&;&&;",
        "abc & def ; ghi",
    ]
    for s in inputs:
        assert unescapeHTML(s) == s


def test_unescapeHTML_entity_with_internal_ampersand():
    """
    The new regex allows '&' inside the entity name, which could cause
    incorrect matches. Ensure such inputs are not transformed.
    """
    # Simulate a malformed entity containing an extra '&'
    input_str = "&amp&foo;"
    # Old regex would stop at the first ';' after '&amp', but there is none,
    # so no match; the string should remain unchanged.
    expected = "&amp&foo;"
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected
